verifiedFacts: Location: Cipanas, Kecamatan Tarogong Kaler, Kabupaten Garut, at the southeastern foot of active stratovolcano Gunung Guntur.
History: Documented by Belgian painter-naturalist Auguste Payen in 1818 ('Tjipanasse') and 1891 colonial travel guides describing natural 38-42°C bamboo bathhouses.
Temperature: Natural geothermal springs emerge at ~40°C to 70°C at source vents and are moderated to ~38-42°C in soaking pools.
Hydrothermal System: Cold rainwater (meteoric water) falls on Gunung Guntur slopes, infiltrates porous volcanic ground and deep tectonic fault fractures (sesar/patahan).
Heating & Buoyancy: At depth, water contacts hot rocks heated conductively by Gunung Guntur's magma chamber; heated lower-density water rises back up through fault conduits.

Clear & Mild-Sulfur Water: Because Cipanas lies in the outflow zone rather than a direct summit crater, fluids undergo hundreds of meters of volcanic rock filtration without direct magmatic acid gas mixing, yielding clear mineral-rich skin-friendly water.
